question: Recent reporting by EUobserver revealed that the Commission Coordinator on combating antisemitism and fostering Jewish life levelled accusations of ‘ambient antisemitism’ at EU staff organising fundraisers, including bake sales, for starving people in Gaza. We have not found any mention in any of the Commission’s documents of the term ‘ambient antisemitism’.

The Coordinator also accused European citizens who have engaged in peaceful protest against Israel’s slaughter in Gaza as being somehow associated with Hamas or other extremist organisations. Moreover, the Coordinator challenged some reports by the UN on the humanitarian situation in Gaza. 1.
Does the Commission consider all fundraisers for charities, such as the Irish Red Cross in the case of the bake sales, to be responsible for ‘ambient antisemitism’?
Does the Commission think it is acceptable for a Commission official to be levelling baseless accusations against EU citizens exercising their peaceful right to protest?
Does the Commission know which UN reports the Coordinator was referring to, and did her comments represent the Commission’s position?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (20.10.2025) The Commission's Coordinator on Combating Antisemitism is carrying out her work in line with the EU Strategy on combating antisemitism and fostering Jewish life.

As regards the question on fundraising, Commission staff, as all EU officials, enjoy the right to freedom of expression in line with the Charter of Fundamental Rights of the European Union1 and the staff regulations2. As it has been recalled constantly by the Court of Justice of the European Union, the right to freedom of expression is exercised with due respect to the principles of loyalty and impartiality.

The Commission authorises in principle occasional social, charity or fundraising activities by staff (e.g. book or bake sales). The EU is a longstanding partner of the United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees in the Near East (UNRWA) and strong supporter of the United Nations’ (UN) work in Gaza and the West Bank.
UN agencies must be able to operate without obstruction in humanitarian crises worldwide.
